description: Adding an agent to an existing drive takes 6 interactions plus a 600px scroll, and the user must hand-feed a recovery file or key even though the console in the same browser may already hold that drive's key. The link that starts the path ('Add to an existing drive instead') is small underlined text beneath a grey note, and the default is a new drive. The form puts Approve below the fold at 1280x800.
expected: When the browser already holds the drive key (console session) offer it as a one-click choice; otherwise a compact form with Approve visible.
actual: Manual selection of drive, then file or paste, then Approve (step-3-existing.png, step-3b-existing-bottom.png).
suggested_fix: Use the key already loaded in the console; shorten the form by moving 'Only allow writes under' and the delegate checkbox into an 'Advanced' disclosure.

description: The recovery-file picker is the browser's native 'Choose File / No file chosen' control and the Drive field is a native select, while the other inputs and buttons use the app's style. Label-to-input spacing is tighter (4px) than the space above each label.
expected: A styled file button matching other controls.
actual: Unstyled native file input inside a bordered box (step-3b-existing-bottom.png).
suggested_fix: Hide the input and style a label as the app's secondary button, showing the chosen file name.

description: Validation errors for the key fields appear in a box above the Approve button, about 450px below the empty field. The fields are not marked invalid and focus stays on the button, so a user who scrolled past the form may not see the message (and the box pushes Approve down). Wrong-file copy says 'The bundle does not contain a key for this drive.' even when the user picked a 'recovery file'.
expected: Inline error next to the field, field marked aria-invalid, focus moved to it; consistent term for the file.
suggested_fix: Render the error under the key field; use 'recovery file or bundle' consistently.

description: After approval the card says 'Approved' in both the heading and the body ('Approved. Return to your agent...') and offers no link to the console or Agents list, so the owner cannot verify the new agent without finding the way back.
expected: One 'Approved' statement plus a link 'View in Agents'.
suggested_fix: Change body to 'Return to your agent; it will finish setup on its own.' and add a console link.

description: On the Agents tab 'Revoke access' is enabled (and styled as a primary bordered button) on agents that already have 0 active keys (old-laptop, trace-a), so the action does nothing useful. Every row carries the same heavy destructive button, which dominates the list; scopes, drives and machines are not shown, so the owner cannot confirm which scopes trace-bot got.
expected: Disable or hide Revoke for 0-key agents; show scopes and drive per agent; quieter destructive styling.
actual: All 10 'Revoke access' buttons enabled (DOM check), rows show only name, id, issuer and key count (step-7-agents.png).
suggested_fix: Disable when activeKeys is 0; show scope chips.

description: Agent rows are different heights (about 100px with an 'issued by' line, 78px without). 'devin', which was handed a drive by research-bot, has no 'issued by' line while trace-c and assistant do, so provenance is inconsistent.
expected: Uniform row height; provenance shown for every handed-off agent.
suggested_fix: Reserve the second line, or record the granting agent for grants.

description: On /connect the delegate checkbox hint sits 11px above the Approve button while other gaps are 24px; the primary button looks glued to the small print.
expected: Consistent gap before the primary action.
